viva.question: Does satisfying the Cauchy-Riemann equations guarantee analyticity?
viva.answer: Only together with continuity of the partial derivatives near the point.
viva.why: The equations alone are necessary but the converse needs the extra continuity hypothesis — see the standard counterexample using sqrt(|xy|).
viva.followUp: Give a function where C-R holds only at an isolated point.
viva.trap: Assuming the equations alone are always sufficient.

viva.question: What's the single biggest consequence of Cauchy's Integral Formula?
viva.answer: Every analytic function is automatically infinitely differentiable — no real-variable analogue exists.
viva.why: The generalized formula gives f^(n) directly as a contour integral for every n, with no extra hypotheses needed.
viva.followUp: Why does this fail for real-differentiable functions?
viva.trap: Assuming complex and real differentiability behave similarly.
